# Note-pull CLI fixtures

These are synthetic vaults. They contain no notes exported from Bryan's vault. The
saved outputs are generated by the real `bob` CLI from the current checkout and are consumed by
`tests/cli/capture/note_pull.rs`; they are suitable for the Bob Mac Capture phase after
this phase closes.

Regenerate every saved output with:

```bash
cargo build --locked --bin bob
python3 tests/fixtures/note_pull/generate.py
```

For release-latency evidence, first open the Bob vault through SASE, then build and run
the benchmark on the path it returns. The script copies Markdown and the Obsidian Tasks
settings into a disposable directory under `target/`, creates a synthetic fixed-day
note there, and removes the entire copy on exit. It never writes to its source checkout.

```bash
SOURCE=$(sase repo open gh:bobs-org/bob -r "Copy the Bob vault for isolated note-pull latency measurement")
cargo build --release --locked --bin bob
python3 tests/fixtures/note_pull/benchmark.py --vault-source "$SOURCE"
```

The script records host, source revision, copied dataset size, the two route sizes,
command, clock, warm-up, sample count, median, p95, maximum, and response codes in
`performance.md`. It measures the largest root-level area/project note and `mac_inbox`.
If a route has no open tasks in the source vault, Bob's `nothing_to_pull_in` refusal is
the measured outcome for that route; other non-success responses fail the benchmark.
The acceptance target is at most 70 ms.

The generator copies each fixture input into a fresh temporary vault, passes `-b` and
`BOB_DAY_FILE` explicitly, and sets `BOB_NOW=2026-10-05 09:30:00`, a missing
`BOB_CONFIG_FILE`, and `NO_COLOR=1`. It saves stdout exactly as emitted by Bob, with
only the temporary vault and day-file paths replaced by `<VAULT>` and `<DAY_FILE>`.
The CLI tests expand those two documented substitutions to their own temporary paths
before comparing JSON, so output keys, offer numbering, status, wording, destination
roles, counts, and omitted fields remain pinned.

| Output | Exact capture arguments after the executable | Exit | Source input |
| --- | --- | ---: | --- |
| `np1/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --dry-run -- @sase` | 0 | `np1/vault/` |
| `np1/human.txt` | `capture -b <vault> --dry-run -- @sase` | 0 | `np1/vault/` |
| `np2/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -p all -- @sase` | 0 | `np2/vault/` |
| `np2/human.txt` | `capture -b <vault> -p all -- @sase` | 0 | `np2/vault/` |
| `np10-empty/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -- @sase` | 2 | `np10-empty/vault/` |
| `np10-folded/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -- @sase` | 2 | `np10-folded/vault/` |
| `np12/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -- @nosuch` | 2 | `np12/vault/` |
| `np13/stdout.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --require-pull-in-choice -- @sase` | 1 | `np13/vault/` |
| `np16/choice.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -p 2 --require-inbox-route-choice -- @mac_inbox` | 1 | `np16/vault/` |
| `np16/routed.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json -p 2 -i 1=health -- @mac_inbox` | 0 | `np16/vault/` |
| `np-move/preview.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --dry-run -- <MOVE_DRAFT>` | 0 | `np-move/vault/` |
| `np-move/picked.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --dry-run -p all -- <MOVE_DRAFT>` | 0 | `np-move/vault/` |
| `np-move/human.txt` | `capture -b <vault> --dry-run -p all -- <MOVE_DRAFT>` | 0 | `np-move/vault/` |
| `np-move/choice.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --require-pull-in-choice -- <MOVE_DRAFT>` | 1 | `np-move/vault/` |
| `np-move/two-notes.json` | `capture -b <vault> -f json --dry-run -- $'@work\n\n@dev'` | 0 | `np-move/vault/` |

`<MOVE_DRAFT>` is `generate.py`'s `MOVE_DRAFT`: `@work`, `@dev`, transfers
`@work+gamma > @bob` and `@dev+delta > @bob`, then a `Docs push` project note
that moves `^beta`. One `@work` pull splits across two destinations, two sources
share `bob.md`, and `@dev`'s only offer moves while its hidden resident keeps
the dev group's fold. Groups follow each row's `offer.note` source; `note_path`
reports the final home.

`sa36_hello_and_plain_x_add_no_relation_snapshot_reads` also includes an ordinary
`@sase` list draft and proves it adds no catalog walk or dependency/relation snapshot
reads. NP1 asserts a dependency-free note pull does not read a dependents snapshot.

The CLI suite verifies unchanged file bytes for previews, choice-required and missing
source refusals, invalid picks, and a failed multi-item draft. NP1 and NP2 human output
is pinned alongside their JSON. NP10 saves both folded-resident and no-open-task
refusals; NP16 saves both the inbox-choice refusal and its routed result.
